concept.name: Fiduciary duty
concept.definition: The obligation, owed under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 by an investment adviser to its client, to act in the client's best interest; per the SEC's 2019 interpretation it comprises a duty of care (including advice in the client's best interest, best execution, and advice and monitoring over the relationship) and a duty of loyalty (not subordinating the client's interests to the adviser's own, with full and fair disclosure of material conflicts).
concept.intuition: A fiduciary must run your money the way a careful, honest trustee would — putting your interests first, telling you about conflicts, and never secretly profiting at your expense.
concept.mechanics: The duty is enforceable through the Advisers Act's antifraud provisions (Section 206) and applies to the ongoing advisory relationship, with its specific content shaped by the scope of the engagement. Duty-of-care failures include unsuitable advice or poor execution; duty-of-loyalty failures include undisclosed conflicts such as revenue sharing or proprietary-product preferences.
concept.failure_modes: Disclosure-based loyalty compliance can devolve into buried boilerplate clients never read; the duty's scope varies with the relationship (a one-time plan vs. continuous management), creating ambiguity; and dual registrants switching hats between adviser and broker roles blur which standard applies when.
concept.misconceptions: Not all financial professionals are fiduciaries — brokers historically owed suitability (now Reg BI best-interest) duties rather than the Advisers Act fiduciary duty; and fiduciary status doesn't eliminate conflicts, it requires managing and disclosing them rather than hiding them.
concept.example: An adviser that sweeps client cash into its affiliate's low-yield money market fund while a higher-yield equivalent exists, without disclosing the affiliation and revenue benefit, breaches its duty of loyalty even if the fund is 'suitable.'

citations.source: SEC, Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers, Investment Advisers Act Release No. 5248, 84 FR 33669
citations.section: Section II: Investment Advisers' Fiduciary Duty
